trust_decision.summary: Whether a pack-entry target path read from the compiled installer's packs.info (after ${VAR} translation) may contain '..' segments before the installer creates directories and writes the file; decided nowhere at the pinned commit — the fix adds it at install time in UnpackerBase.unpack(PackFile,...) and at compile time in the PackFile constructor.

landing_point.why: The advisory names UnpackerBase and 'malicious pack entries'; unpack(PackFile,...) translates getTargetPath() and immediately builds the File, creates directories and extracts.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The installer-side check already blocks traversal at extraction time, and the compiler runs on the installer author's own trusted descriptor, so a solver can argue that validating PackFile at compile time (and the override-rename / parsable paths) is redundant or 'not a pack entry'.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Pack entries may legitimately target absolute paths outside INSTALL_PATH (e.g. /etc/myapp/config.properties); the fix only logs an AUDIT warning for these and the fix's test requires them to keep installing. A 'must stay under INSTALL_PATH' fix breaks this; regular nested targets like subdir/file.txt must also keep working.
